data_quality_assurance:
Data quality will be ensured through:

Standardised  procedures at RTU, repeated measurements, and documented protocols.

Model verification and validation, including parameter checks, sensitivity analysis, and expert review with UPV and TalTech.

Use of trusted sources (peer-reviewed literature, Eurostat, EC CRM datasets) and a consistent coding protocol for all extracted data.

Accurate and anonymised transcription of interviews, applying a structured coding approach for reliability.

Comprehensive documentation (data dictionaries, workflows, version control) to ensure transparency and reproducibility.

Supervisor oversight and internal checks for completeness, correctness, and consistency before data release.
dataset.description:
The research generates data related to the economic and environmental evaluation of critical raw materials (CRMs) reused from secondary resources within powder metallurgy.
The data include:

Literature review datasets with coded variables on CRM supply chains, recycling technologies, and policy frameworks.

Comparative datasets on CRM performance in different reuse scenarios.

Data will be created by the PhD candidate and collaborating at RTU, TalTech, and UPV.
The main purpose of the data is to evaluate CRM reuse efficiency and develop models, decision-support tools, and policy recommendations for sustainable material recovery.

dmp.description:
This research focuses on evaluating the economic and ecological efficiency of reusing critical raw materials (CRMs), particularly metal-based CRMs, derived from secondary resources within powder metallurgy.
The study integrates life cycle assessment (LCA), techno-economic analysis (TEA), and system dynamics modelling to develop a unified methodology for assessing CRM recycling potential. It addresses key barriers such as technological limitations, high processing costs, insufficient information about CRM content in end-of-life products, and gaps in policy and regulatory frameworks.
The research aims to provide comparative efficiency models, scenario analyses, and policy recommendations for sustainable CRM recovery.
